7.Summary description of the proposed organizational change The College of Engineering proposes establishing a standalone Department of Biomedical Engineering Electrical,Computer,and Biomedical Engineering(ECBE).A standalone B ME department will elevate program visibility,strengthen student recruitment and enrollment,support faculty recruitment and retention,and promote stronger research collaborations and industry partnerships.
B.RATIONALE There should be a demonstrable purpose and documented need for the proposed organizational change. 1.
Explain why the organizational change is being proposed.
Biomedical engineering is a rapidly expanding interdisciplinary field bridging engineering, biology, and medicine.URl's B ME program has strong undergraduate enrollment,successful graduates,and faculty conducting nationally funded research in areassuch as wearable bio sensing,brain- machine interfaces,and neural robotics.Despite these successes,the program's administrative integration with EC BE limits its visibility,ability to tailor curricula,and competitiveness in recruiting faculty and students.

Establishing a standalone department will address these limitations, align with industry and workforce needs,and strengthen URl's role in biomedical research and education.
Theneed fora standalone Department of Biomedical Engineering at URl is reinforced by direct feedback from our key stakeholders and comparisons with peer institutions.Our graduates consistently emphasize the value of a clear,independent B ME identity,noting that it would strengthen their professional preparation,enhance visibility for research opportunities,and better position them inthe competitive job market.Similarly,members of research partners have recommended the establishment of an independent department as away to foster stronger industry and academic collaborations, attract high-caliber faculty, and provide a more focused administrative and organizational structure to support growth.

In addition,a review of peer and aspirational institutions shows that independent BME departments are the norm.Remaining administratively within EC BE places URl at a competitive disadvantage in student recruitment,faculty hiring,and research prominence.Creatinga standalone department addresses these gaps, aligning URl with national standards and ensuring the program can continue to thrive as a leader in biomedical engineering education and research.
C.INSTITUTIONAL ROLE The organizational change should be clearly related to the published role and mission of the institution and be compatible with the organizational structure of the institution. 1.Explain how the organizational change is consistent with the published role and mission of the institution and how it is related to institutional planning.
The creation of a standalone Department of Biomedical Engineering directly supports URl's mission to foster innovation, advance interdisciplinary research, and prepare graduates to meet the needs of aglobal society.It builds on existing strengths in engineering,health sciences,and statewide biomedical initiatives,aligning with institutional planning priorities and strategic goals.

2.Explain how the organizational change impacts other units and programs within the institution.
How have you communicated with the other units and programs about this proposed change, and what were the concerns raised relative to the organizational change?
The proposed organizational change to establish a standalone Department of Biomedical Engineering will have minimal impact on other units and programs within URl.The B ME program already exists aspart of Ec BE, and this transition does not reduce resources or capacity for other departments.Instead,it provides greater clarity in administrative structure and enhances opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration acrossthe Collegeof Engineering and the broader university.

It will enhance interdisciplinary engagement through joint faculty appointments with units such as Kin es i ology,the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program(INP),and the Health Sciences,supporting shared teaching,co-advised students,and collaborative research across bio mechanics,neuroscience,rehabilitation,and translational health technologies.The department will also promote shared use of core facilities and research infrastructure,maximizing institutional resources and fostering cross-unit innovation.
Communication regarding the proposed organizational change has been ongoing and multi-level.
Discussions have taken place with faculty and leadership within ECBE,aswell as with other engineering departments,including Mechanical Engineering and Industrial Engineering.

Engagement has also occurred with the INP, Kin es i ology, and relevant health-related units through faculty meetings,individual consultations,advisory input,and regulars take holder updates.These conversations have helped shape the proposed structure and identify opportunities for collaboration and alignment.As a result of these discussions,wehave received support from ECBE,Kin es i ology,Mathematics and Mathematical Sciences,Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program, and the Dean of the College of Engineering.
Overall,the proposed organizational change is designed to strengthen—not compete with—other expanding shared research opportunities,and creatinga transparent framework for resource planning.The establishment of a standalone B ME department is expected to enhance institutional cohesion and advance URl's broader goals in health,biomedical science, and interdisciplinary education.

Instead, the independent department will strengthen URl's competitive position regionally and nationally,potentially attracting students who might otherwise seek programs out of state.In developing the proposal,biomedical engineering departments and curricula at peer and aspirational universities were closely evaluated and discussed among BME faculty to ensure alignment with national norms and best practices.These evaluations informed

M.S. and Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering).
